claims.statement: James Mace wrote in a card that he would only whip Tom Allen for the reputation and battle-money of their meeting, with no international character to it.
claims.excerpt: any international character. I, at least, can see none, and only propose to whip Mr. Tom Allen

claims.statement: Mace said an item in the St. Louis Evening Dispatch had evidently been inserted at Tom Allen's request as an advertisement of his own pretensions.
claims.excerpt: an item evidently msertes at the request of Mr. Tom Aller

claims.statement: An item apparently from Tom Allen in the Dispatch described him, as a citizen, as champion of the United States.
claims.excerpt: Allen, (now acitizen,) who is champion of the United States

claims.statement: Tom Allen complained that Mace had not called on him.
claims.excerpt: He complains that I have not called upon him.

claims.statement: James Mace said Tom Allen was as much an Englishman as himself and had been in America little longer than Mace.
claims.excerpt: much an Englishman aa myself, has been here little longer than I

notes: Card is dated 'March 23, 1876' in the OCR; 1870 fits the paper date. These are Mace's claims about Allen, one side of a dispute. 'aa' in the excerpt is OCR for 'as'.
